mem.7:
Caroline and Melanie (“Mel”; surnames unknown) are friends who catch up periodically. Caroline is transgender and from Sweden; she moved away around 2019. As of June 9, 2023, she had been transitioning for three years (since about 2020). Melanie is married with children; as of June 9, 2023, she had been married five years (wedding around 2018; exact date unknown).

**May 8, 2023:** Melanie was swamped with work and children. Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group the previous day. Hearing other trans people’s stories helped her feel accepted and more courageous about embracing herself. She planned to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health work to help people with similar experiences; Melanie said her empathy would make her a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall painted with a woman; Melanie liked the painting. Melanie shared her 2022 painting of a sunrise over a lake, special to her; painting helps her express feelings, be creative, and relax. Caroline praised the colors. Caroline left to do research; Melanie went swimming with her children.

**May 25:** Melanie had run a mental-health charity race on Saturday, May 20. It was rewarding and thought-provoking, prompting reflection on well-being and self-care. She tries to make time for herself daily by running, reading, or playing violin; these refresh and ground her, help her be present for family, and self-care remains a work in progress. Her children were excited for summer break; family was considering June camping. Caroline was researching adoption agencies. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She shared a photo of an adoption-agency sign/building and felt hopeful despite much to absorb. She hoped to adopt as a single parent and was considering agencies supportive of LGBTQ+ adopters. Melanie said she would be an awesome mom and provide love and stability.

**June 9:** Caroline had spoken at a school event the previous week about her trans journey, struggles and growth since coming out, and encouraged students to participate in the LGBTQ community. She felt powerful; audience members related and were inspired to become better allies. She believes conversations about gender identity and inclusion foster understanding, acceptance, and hope. Melanie praised her courage and advocacy. Caroline had received much love and support and wanted to pass it on, use her voice for change, and build a hopeful community. Both wanted to support one another and make a positive difference. Melanie said her husband and children motivate and support her. Caroline calls friends, family, and mentors her “rocks”; she had known them for four years, since moving from Sweden, and they were especially important after a difficult breakup. Their love, guidance, acceptance, and encouragement helped her accept and grow into her true self and were instrumental in her transition. Family is everything to Caroline; loved ones make her happy and grateful. She shared a photo of a family posing in a yard. Melanie said she’d been married five years and shared a wedding photo of herself in a dress holding a bouquet. She also shared photos described as a man and little girl in front of a waterfall (pictured people not explicitly identified) and a man and woman sitting on a blanket eating. A family outing included games and good food; Melanie cherishes family time and feels alive and happy with them.

**June 27:** Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and heart, given by her grandmother in Sweden when Caroline was young. It represents love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. Melanie shared patterned bowls. Caroline treasures a hand-painted bowl a friend made for her 18th birthday, ten years earlier; its pattern and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Melanie’s family had camped in the mountains the previous week (around June 19): they explored nature, hiked, roasted marshmallows around a campfire; the view from the top was amazing and her two younger children love nature. Caroline was exploring counseling/mental-health work, possibly with trans people, to support self-acceptance and mental health. On June 23 she attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on therapeutic methods and working well with trans people. She admired professionals’ commitment to safe spaces and hoped to create an inviting, safe place where people could grow, informed by her own journey and support. She shared a bookshelf photo; Melanie also shared a bookshelf photo.

**July 3:** Caroline had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week (roughly June 26–July 2). The happy crowd made her feel she belonged, showed community growth, and motivated her to help others through her story. She remained interested in counseling/mental health. Melanie signed up for a pottery class on July 2; pottery feels therapeutic, calming, creative, and emotionally expressive, and brings her joy. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and a photo of a bowl with a black-and-white flower design she made in class and was proud of. Caroline praised it and said she was learning piano. Caroline planned to attend a transgender conference in July and promised an update.

**July 6:** Caroline was continuing to explore counseling/mental-health work; helping people and making a positive impact felt both tough and rewarding. Melanie took her children to a museum on July 5 and shared a photo of two children playing in a water-play area. They loved the dinosaur exhibit, learning about animals, and thought the bones were cool; it reminded Melanie why she loves being a mom. Caroline is building a library for future children and looks forward to reading to them and opening their minds; it includes children’s classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She shared a bookcase photo with books and toys. Melanie’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*, for its friendship and compassion, and she shared a cover photo showing a girl and cat. Caroline had picnicked with friends the previous week and shared a photo of women on a blanket in a park. Melanie asked how friends helped her transition; Caroline described their unconditional love, guidance, acceptance, and encouragement. Melanie affirmed the importance of unconditional love and shared a photo of her family around a beach campfire; beach camping brings them closer.

**July 12:** Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference two days earlier (July 10), met people with similar journeys, felt totally accepted, and was grateful for the community. She wants to fight for trans rights and spread awareness; though LGBTQ rights have advanced, she sees more progress needed. She is still looking into counseling/mental-health jobs because she wants people to have someone to talk to. Her own mental-health struggles and helpful support inspired this goal. Melanie praised her and shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin, saying a book she read the previous year reminds her to pursue dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her discover herself. Her favorite is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it helped her feel connected and hopeful. She learned self-acceptance, finding support, and that tough times pass; she also said pets bring joy. Melanie shared photos of two little girls with a dog and a cat lying on the floor. She has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; they are sweet, playful, and brighten the home. Melanie also shared photos of pink/purple running shoes and said she had been running farther since their last chat to destress and improve her headspace. Caroline encouraged her to keep prioritizing mental health; Melanie said running had improved it and she would continue.

CAROLINE
Values advocacy, art, and LGBTQ+ community. LGBTQ groups, conferences, workshops, youth-center activities and Pride conversations inspired her to help others and explore counseling/mental-health work (career interest noted 2023-06-27). Joined “Connected LGBTQ Activists,” mentors a trans teen, and took the teen to a June 2023 Pride event; seeing the teen’s face light up was a highlight. Poetry reading on 2023-10-06 was a safe, empowering space. Classroom poster and “Trans Lives Matter” sign photos; described atmosphere as electric with support/energy. Sunflowers mean warmth/happiness; roses love/beauty.

Treasures cross-and-heart necklace from Swedish grandmother (love, faith, strength, roots, family support) and hand-painted bowl from friend for her 18th birthday, around 2013. Guinea pig Oscar likes vegetables, especially parsley. Learning piano; builds a library for future children (classics, multicultural/educational books); likes *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt. Loves reading for guidance, motivation and self-discovery. Enjoys nature, hiking, biking and picnics. Upset by religious-conservative encounter on a hike; supportive people reassure her. On 2023-09-09–10 biked with friends, saw beach sunset, called it refreshing; photo showed beach, fence, sunset.

MELANIE
Married about five years as of 2023-06-09. Two younger children; family is central. Dog and cat are Luna and Oliver (conversation doesn’t specify which name belongs to which); both sweet/playful, brighten home and make family smile. Enjoys running, reading, violin, clarinet (learned young; self-expression/relaxation), painting and pottery. Running relieves stress; ran mental-health charity race 2023-05-20. Learning self-care helps her care for family; work in progress. Favorite childhood book *Charlotte’s Web*. Best wedding part was marrying partner and promising to stay together; flowers in decor.

Family enjoys camping, forest walks, mountain hikes, beaches, museums, swimming, pottery and parks. Children love nature; museum visit 2023-07-05: excited by dinosaurs, loved learning about animals and thought bones were cool; Melanie said it reminded her why she loves motherhood. June 2023 mountain camping included hiking, marshmallows and summit view. Family looks forward to summer camping, roasting marshmallows, stories by campfire and enjoying each other. Both said happy moments and friendship make hardship bearable, always there for each other. Caroline shared friends with balloons, recalling prior Pride. Discussed summer outing/trip, perhaps nature; no date/place chosen.

Aug 23 — Caroline applied to adoption agencies after attending adoption advice/assistance group; first step toward motherhood, excited and nervous about responsibility. Shared sign with guinea pig picture. Her guinea pig Oscar likes parsley/vegetables; shared photo eating parsley. Mel has Oliver and cat Bailey; Oliver once hid a bone in her slipper. Mel shared photo captioned Oliver but described as black dog with frisbee. Mel had fed a horse a carrot; Caroline loved childhood horseback riding with her dad through fields and wind. Mel shared horse painting on wooden wall; likes painting animals, finds it peaceful and special. Caroline shared blue-faced self-portrait made previous week; felt liberated/empowered, art helps explore identity and is therapeutic. Wants authentic life and to help others do same through supportive people and LGBTQ-rights advocacy. Mel wished her well on adoption journey and offered support.

Names: Caroline and Melanie (surname not provided).
mem.19:
Caroline and Melanie (“Mel”; surname unknown) are friends who regularly encourage and support each other. Dates are in 2023 unless stated otherwise.

CAROLINE
- Began transitioning around 2020; moved from her home country around 2019. Came out after a breakup and has spoken at school about being trans, her struggles and growth. Friends’ reactions varied. Friends, family and mentors helped her through transition and self-acceptance.
- Treasures a cross-and-heart necklace her grandmother gave her in childhood in Sweden; it symbolizes love, faith, strength, roots and family support. Also treasures a friend’s hand-painted bowl from her 18th birthday.
- Long dreamed of becoming a single adoptive parent. Researched agencies, chose an LGBTQ+-friendly agency, attended an adoption council on July 14, and contacted an adoption mentor by October 13. On October 20, said she felt ready to be a mom and share her love. Built a bookcase for future children, with classics and multicultural/educational books. Advised Mel to research agencies/lawyers, collect references and financial/medical documents, and prepare emotionally for the wait.
- On October 20, passed the adoption agency interviews the previous Friday, October 13; was excited and grateful this was a major step toward having a family. Wants to give children who have lacked a home a safe, loving place, with love and acceptance. Sees adoption as giving back. Her own long journey to self-acceptance and the support she received motivate her to help others; bringing comfort and helping people grow brings her joy.
- Favorite book: Amy Ellis Nutt’s *Becoming Nicole*, which gave her connection and hope. Loves reading; books offer guidance, motivation and self-discovery. On July 12, a book-cover photo Mel shared reminded Caroline to keep going and never give up. Pets bring her joy; blue is relaxing.
- Attended LGBTQ+ support group May 8; felt accepted and braver, considered further study/counseling. Attended LGBTQ counseling workshop June 23 and considered counseling, perhaps for trans people. Mentored a trans teen, volunteered at an LGBTQ youth center, shared her story to help young people feel less alone, and joined Connected LGBTQ Activists. Attended Pride and an LGBTQ conference July 10; felt belonging and wanted to advocate for trans rights and mental health. Planned August LGBTQ art show and September talent show. Attended transgender poetry reading October 6; described a safe, empowering, supportive atmosphere where trans people shared stories.
- Shared classroom-poster photo, “Trans Lives Matter” sign, and drawing of a woman in a dress; drawing represented freedom, authenticity and embracing womanhood.
- Art helps her process emotions, explore/accept gender identity and preserve happy moments. Has made art since around age 17; open to pottery. Work explores trans experience, identity, body and self-acceptance. “Embracing Identity”: woman in red with cow in her lap, symbolizing comfort, love and acceptance. Other works: liberating blue-faced self-portrait; rainbow mural (trans courage); eagle (freedom/resilience); stained-glass person with key (inner potential); changing stained glass (growth); red/blue painting rejecting rigid gender binaries. Likes drawing flowers. Tree/bright-sun painting meant unity and strength; heart painting meant togetherness and empowerment. Recently tried abstract art for free, unplanned emotional expression. Busy painting; finished a sunset painting inspired by beach visit sometime August 18–24; watching the sun dip below the horizon and its colors felt amazing and calming, and she wanted to capture that feeling.
- Plays and sings, mostly acoustic guitar (started around 2018). Sara Bareilles’ “Brave” represents courage and progress.
- Biked with friends September 9–10, saw a beach sunset, and described the day as refreshing. Shared beach/fence/sunset photo. A hike with religious conservatives upset her; supportive people reassure her.

MELANIE
- Married about five years as of June 9 (since approximately 2018); values family, has husband and children including a son and daughter. Shared photos of husband/children. Treasures youngest child’s first steps; favorite memory is marrying her partner. Childhood favorite book: *Charlotte’s Web*.
- Pets: dog Luna and cat Oliver. Family enjoys camping and beach trips, campfires, marshmallows and stories; favorite memory includes wishing on Perseid meteors. Camped in mountains in June, hiked and roasted marshmallows. Family volunteered at a homeless shelter.
- On July 5, took children to a museum. They were excited by dinosaur exhibit, loved learning about animals and thought bones were cool; Mel said the outing reminded her why she loves being a mother.
- Ran a mental-health charity race; aims for daily self-care (running, reading or violin), though it remains a work in progress. Likes live music; “Summer Sounds” played upbeat pop. Plays clarinet, started young; likes Bach, Mozart and Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect.”
- Began pottery July 2; finds clay calming and expressive. Art/painting is healing and a sanctuary; likes landscapes/still life and had painted about seven years. Shared black-and-white flower bowl; blue vase with sunflowers/roses; sunflower painting; calming pink-sky sunset; abstract painting with blue streaks symbolizing tranquility. Flowers mean joy, growth and beauty and were wedding décor. Planned autumn painting. Injured herself in September and paused pottery; said she was doing okay, reading a book Caroline recommended and painting.
- Friend adopted in 2022 after a long process and was happy, prompting Mel to consider adoption. On October 13, Caroline congratulated her and advised preparation.
- Likes unplugged family time, children’s milestones, parks and concerts (including taking daughter to Matt Patterson concert). Shared wedding, greenhouse and beach photos. Also shared a photo described as a man and woman sitting on a blanket eating food; said family played games, ate good food and spent time together, and family moments make life enjoyable.

OCTOBER 20 CONVERSATION
- Mel said a family road trip the previous weekend began with a frightening car accident involving her son; he was okay. Shared photo of car dashboard, white cloth and steering wheel. Accident reminded her life is precious and to cherish family. Children were scared; parents reassured them their brother would be okay. Mel called children tough and resilient, wished she were as resilient, and said they give her strength to keep going. Family are her biggest motivation, support and “rock.”
- Family enjoyed Grand Canyon; shared photo of two children on rocky cliff overlooking canyon. The day before October 20, she took kids on a trail walk to relax after trip; shared photo of woman and child walking on trail and said they loved it.
- Nature helps Mel reset and recharge. Loves family camping for presence, bonding over stories, campfires and nature; waking to birds and fresh air refreshes her soul. Shared sunset over water. Caroline expressed sympathy and relief son was okay, and agreed loved ones and nature are precious/restorative.

OCTOBER 22 CONVERSATION
- Mel shared photo of wooden dolls/figurines she had bought October 21; they reminded her of family love, and she asked Caroline’s future vision.
- Caroline said she wanted to build her own family and provide a roof for children who had not had one; adoption is a way to give back and show love and acceptance. Mel affirmed all children deserve a loving home. Caroline wants a safe, loving home where children experience love and acceptance, and said finding self-acceptance was a long process. She credited friends, family and role models with helping her discover who she is and wants to pass support on.
- Mel praised Caroline’s strength and inspiration; both valued being there for each other and being oneself. Caroline shared a green-and-yellow-design clock photo, then a painting with “happiness” painted on it.
